name: BayEngage: Email Marketing
author: bayengage

sections.description:
Made for Woocommerce Stores
BayEngage email marketing app has a secure and seamless integration process. This means easy navigation and no learning curve. This app is designed to save time for Woocommerce merchants and all the UI options are designed similar to Woocommerce.

BayEngage Features

Get access to 250+ free email templates
Design your next email campaign using one of our 250 free email templates. All these templates have fully loaded professionally designed images and content. They are mobile-responsive and fully customizable.

The templates collection span across 47+ categories, industries, and holidays. Email templates are available for all the holidays such as Thanksgiving, Black Friday, Cyber Monday, Christmas, New Year, Valentines Day, July 4th, Labor Day, and more.

Drag and drop email designer with image editing capabilities
1. Use our drag and drop email designer to design 100% mobile optimized email templates
2. Use our image editing capabilities to apply filters to the images, crop the images and add overlay text
3. Maintain all your photos in one place.

Get access to millions of free stock photos
Create good-looking marketing emails using our free stock images. The in-built stock asset library gives you access to millions of images.

These stock images are free and ready to use with our free and paid plans. These photos can be edited using the drag and drop editor.

Segmentation:
Create segments and send targeted campaigns to increase open rates.

You can create segments based on audience demography, transactional, and behavioral activities.

With BayEngage, you can create segments for:
1. Shopping activity (Loyal customers with more than three orders)
2. Email activity (Engaged customers who opened your recent campaigns)
3. Location filter (Filter customers based on city, state, and zip code)

With BayEngage, you can personalize your email campaigns and make them highly targeted.

Automation:
Save time and effort by automating your critical eCommerce workflows with BayEngage. There are a bunch of automation recipes on BayEngage:

  • Welcome Series
  • Cart Abandonment Recovery
  • Checkout Abandonment Recovery
  • Post-purchase
  • Win back
  • Order confirmation

You can set up email triggers, time delays, and add filters to maximize your ROI through email marketing automation.

Signup forms:
Grow your subscriber base with signup forms. BayEngage has a huge collection of well-designed signup form templates that make it easy for you to pick the one you like, customize, and publish.

You can also set target rules and customize the timing, frequency, and more.

Coupons:
With BayEngage, you can promote your unique static and dynamic discount codes through email marketing and drive more conversions.

SMS Marketing:
BayEngage also has SMS marketing that can help you tap in to this channel and maximize SMS marketing ROI.

BayReviews

This plugin includes a BayReviews module (the bayreviews/ directory) that renders
BayReviews widgets on your storefront. It is off by default and is enabled under
WooCommerce -> Settings -> BayEngage -> “BayReviews Widgets”.

What it does when enabled:

  1. Renders widget placeholders for product reviews, product statistics, Q&A,
    collection star ratings and business reviews.
  2. Loads a remote script bundle from sf-rv.bayengage.com, which fills those
    placeholders in the browser.
  3. Passes the following to that bundle: store domain, product id, product name,
    product image and URL, stock status, the WordPress user id and display name of a
    logged-in shopper (or the BayEngage tracking session id for guests), and the order
    id when a customer arrives from an order confirmation link. Customer email
    addresses are not included.
sections.installation:
1. Upload BayEngage: Email Marketing to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory
    2, Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress
  2. Navigate to BayEngage Sign Up Page.
  3. You need to create an account
  4. After create an account you need to accept scopes
  5. When you accept Import will start and redirect to https://app.bayengage.com/dashboard
  6. You are done!
    Note: For further support please write to support@targetbay.com
sections.changelog:
2.1.0

  • Changed: the storefront tracking payload (_be) once again includes the logged-in
    customer’s email address as tr_email, as it did in 2.0.7 and earlier. It is empty
    for guests.

2.0.9

  • New: BayReviews widgets can now be enabled from WooCommerce -> Settings -> BayEngage
    with the “BayReviews Widgets” checkbox. Widgets are off by default.
  • Changed: the BayReviews module is loaded from the main plugin file and only hooks into
    the storefront when the setting is enabled.
  • Removed: the separate BayReviews settings tab and its unused settings; the single
    toggle in the BayEngage tab replaces them.
  • Documented the BayReviews module in this readme.

2.0.8

  • Security: removed a block that disabled Secure and HttpOnly on the site’s PHP session
    cookie for every request.
  • Security: the cart tracking cookie is now Secure and HttpOnly and expires after 7 days
    instead of 30. The cart_total, be_base_url and raw email cookies are no longer set.
  • Security: stop writing customer email addresses to localStorage and to the _be cookie,
    and stop writing customer email addresses and session ids to the WooCommerce log.
  • Security: added a capability check and CSRF state token to the BayEngage connect flow.
  • Security: the /be-plugin/v1/user-email endpoint now requires a valid nonce, is rate
    limited per IP, and no longer trusts a browser-supplied cookie for the tracking session id.
  • Security: customer role data is no longer exposed as a raw serialized capabilities blob
    in the WooCommerce REST API.
  • Security: escape the stored BayEngage tenant id before it is written into storefront
    markup, and validate its format at the point it is stored.
  • Security: the SMS opt-in checkbox no longer posts the shopper’s email and phone number
    from the browser to a remote endpoint. It calls this site instead, and the plugin
    forwards the result, so the BayEngage endpoint and store identifier are no longer
    published in the page.
  • Fixed: unticking the SMS opt-in box now reports the withdrawal. Previously only opting
    in was ever sent, so consent could not be revoked from the checkout page.
  • Fixed: toggling the SMS opt-in box repeatedly no longer sends a request each time.
  • Fixed: SMS opt-in consent is stored via the order object, so it displays correctly with
    High-Performance Order Storage enabled. The consent timestamp, IP address and the exact
    wording shown are now recorded against the order.
  • Fixed: the SMS opt-in script is only loaded on checkout, and only when the opt-in is
    enabled.
  • Fixed: the checkout email was posted on every blur of the field, including when nothing
    had changed. It is now sent only when the address actually changes, and repeat sends for
    the same session are dropped server-side.
  • Fixed: add-to-cart, cart update and checkout events could each fire more than once per
    action. Emptying a cart is now reported instead of being silently skipped.
  • Fixed: the cart cookie and tracking session are now cleared once an order is placed.
  • Fixed: PHP notices on non-product pages and a deprecated user id property access.
  • Performance: BayEngage webhooks are now non-blocking with a 2 second timeout, so a slow
    or unreachable BayEngage no longer delays add-to-cart, cart updates or checkout.

2.0.7

  • Fix _be cookie format to restore URL-encoded JSON for tracking compatibility
  • Fix be_cookie_* setting timing for servers without output buffering

2.0.6

  • Fix cookie setting issue for servers without output buffering
  • Cookies now set before HTTP output begins ensuring compatibility with all hosting environments
  • Fix _be cookie format to prevent JSON parse errors in tracking scripts

1.7.1

  • Fix Paypal Simulate issue

1.4.0

  • Fix woocommerce add to cart
  • Bug fix

1.2.3

  • Session Issue
  • Bug fix

1.2.2

  • Bug fix

1.2.1

  • The “after checkout billing form” event is customised to handle Abandon cart email for guest user.
  • Technical Note: event name – “woocommerce_after_checkout_billing_form”

1.2.0

  • The “before checkout form” event is customised to handle existing user mapping for the order.
  • Technical Note: event name – “woocommerce_before_checkout_form”

1.1.9

  • Abandon Cart automation data is synced with BayEngage even when the user has a single page checkout flow
